title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1970 work on Dieudonné theory via crystals, which led to 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970/74) and his ICM 1970 talk. The base S is of characteristic p and S_gr is most likely the big ('gros') site of S. Earlier pages define two kinds of 'structures', a) and b). The next page shows that b) consists of a Dieudonné crystal (𝓜, F_𝓜, V_𝓜) together with complexes ℓ. whose cohomology gives locally free pieces. These are ω (the Hodge or cotangent part), t' and ν', which filter M = ε*(𝓜) and are compatible with the Frobenius pullback φ*. This page is a list of open questions about these categories.

(a) Do the categories of structures a) and b) form stacks (champs) on S_gr? This asks whether the data satisfy descent, in the fppf or big-site sense.

(b) There is an 'infinitesimal' functor from 𝒞 into b), going towards Dieudonné crystals M on Sch/F_p. Here 𝒞 is probably the category of truncated BT groups, or the complexes giving them. Is this functor faithful? This is an early form of the question whether the crystalline Dieudonné functor is faithful or fully faithful.

(c) Consider the natural functor from locally free modules ω on S_gr equipped with F_ω and V_ω to the structures a), b). Is it fully faithful? Grothendieck notes it is faithful. Is it at least fully faithful on the subcategory F_ω = 0, or when Ker F = Im V? In modern terms:
- F = 0 corresponds to group schemes of height ≤ 1. These are classified by locally free p-Lie algebras (SGA 3 VIIA). V: ω → ω^(p) is dual to the p-power map on Lie(G).
- Ker F = Im V is the BT_1 (truncated level-1 Barsotti–Tate) condition, which the next page treats.

(d) Can one attach to (ω, F_ω, V_ω) a finite locally free group scheme over S? This would be an inverse to the Dieudonné-type functor.

The marginal note answers one of these: 'yes, if one knows that H^1_cris(𝒞) = H^1_dR(𝒞) and that t*, ω* are locally free'. This conditions an affirmative answer on crystalline cohomology agreeing with de Rham cohomology and on local freeness of the tangent and cotangent pieces.

Overall, the page is a programme of questions about classifying finite flat group schemes killed by p (especially BT_1) over a general base of characteristic p by semilinear algebra data.
errors: No outright error on this page; these are questions. However, the line of reasoning they lead into on the next page ('Cela détermine ω de façon unique', deduced from φ*(n) = φ*(ω)) is only valid when S is reduced, or when Frobenius-twisted subbundles determine subbundles. Over a non-reduced base such as k[ε], the absolute Frobenius kills the infinitesimal information. By Grothendieck–Messing, distinct deformations of a BT_1 over k[ε] share the same Dieudonné crystal with F and V; the Hodge filtration is extra data. So full faithfulness or unique recovery questions of type (c)/(d) have negative answers over general non-reduced bases. This matches the later restriction of positive results (Berthelot–Messing, de Jong) to reduced or formally smooth bases with p-bases.
Faithfulness claimed in the NB of (c) is plausible but not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Asking whether categories of Dieudonné-type structures (crystals with F, V and Hodge-type filtrations) form stacks on the big site of S
ideas.modern_name: Descent / stack property of Dieudonné crystals and displays
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Grothendieck's Montréal lectures; Berthelot–Breen–Messing (1982)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974)

ideas.what: Faithfulness / full faithfulness of the crystalline Dieudonné functor from (truncated) BT groups to crystals on Sch/F_p
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's full faithfulness problem for the crystalline Dieudonné functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Posed by Grothendieck (ICM 1970, Montréal 1970); solved in cases by Berthelot–Messing, de Jong (1995), and later Lau

ideas.what: Subcategory F = 0 (height-one groups) as a test case, with V on ω dual to the p-power map on Lie
ideas.modern_name: Classification of height-one finite group schemes by p-Lie algebras

ideas.modern_name: BT_1 ↔ F-zips / truncated displays / Dieudonné modules mod p

ideas.what: Constructing a finite locally free group scheme from (ω, F_ω, V_ω), conditional on H^1_cris = H^1_dR and local freeness of t*, ω*
ideas.modern_name: Inverse Dieudonné functor over general bases of characteristic p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Open in general; partial results by de Jong, Lau, Lau–Zink

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the functor from linear-algebra data (ω, F_ω, V_ω) to Dieudonné structures is fully faithful on the subcategory F = 0 and on Ker F = Im V. He also asks whether such data produce a finite locally free group scheme over an arbitrary S. This anticipates the later F-zip and truncated-display classification of BT_1 over general bases. Since these threads were later taken up (Moonen–Wedhorn, Lau–Zink), it is a historical anticipation rather than a missed result.
missed.quote: l'est-il du moins sur la sous-catégorie définie par F_ω = 0; l'est-il si Ker F = Im V ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck in 1970 already isolated the BT_1 (Ker F = Im V) and height-one cases as test cases for a Dieudonné classification over general bases. This is of historical interest for crediting the F-zip / truncated-display programme.

deep.surprise_reason: A list of research questions on Dieudonné crystals and BT_1 groups consistent with Grothendieck's publicly posed 1970 problems. The specific test cases (F = 0, Ker F = Im V) are a mildly interesting unpublished detail but were later developed by others.
transcription_corrections: 'S_gr' is most likely Grothendieck's notation for the big ('gros') site of S.
'(NB il est fidèle)' is correct (the 'UB' reading in the image is 'NB').

The insertion in (b) reads '(de 𝒞 dans b))'.
The struck word after 'du moins' appears to be 'si F=0' (replaced by the 'sur la sous-catégorie définie par F_ω = 0' clause).
